subject: how to save more than 30000 factor score in a separate file?

messages.author: 0dad901c56b39cd8
messages.subject: how to save more than 30000 factor score in a separate file?
parts:
Hell, 
I just conducted a CFA using lavaan, i need to use the factor scores for further analysis. However, since I have more than 30,000 cases, Lavaan only shows part of the factor scores, I am wondering how can I save the scores to a separate file that I can open? 
I was told to write in the following way, however, it did not work: 

factorscore<-lavPredict(fit)
write.csv(factorscore,"C:\Users\Researcher\desktop\")   

Could you please tell me how exactly I should write the syntax? 

Thank you very much!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: how to save more than 30000 factor score in a separate file?
parts: since I have more than 30,000 cases, Lavaan only shows part of the factor scores,

lavaan returns all factor scores for cases with complete data.  It is R, not lavaan, that has a default print method set to trim large output sent to the console.  You can find help for general R questions on stack overflow, where you can find a solution to this:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/6758727/how-to-increase-the-limit-for-max-print-in-r

I am wondering how can I save the scores to a separate file that I can open? 
I was told to write in the following way, however, it did not work: 

factorscore<-lavPredict(fit)
write.csv(factorscore,"C:\Users\Researcher\desktop\")   

Could you please tell me how exactly I should write the syntax?

As the ?write.csv help page says, the second argument should be a file name, not just a path for where to put the file.  Also, R expects forward slashes, not the backslashes that only Windows uses to separate (sub)directories in a path. 

write.csv(factorscore,"C:/Users/Researcher/desktop/scores.csv")
